extracted.intended_audience: utility companies, cable system operators, providers of telecommunications services, broadband deployers (attachers), industry counsel, and FCC staff
extracted.subtask_description: Federal Communications Commission rulemaking establishing procedures to expedite resolution of pole attachment disputes that impede or delay broadband deployment, including creation of the Rapid Broadband Assessment Team (RBAT), criteria for Accelerated Docket placement, information-sharing requirements, and clarifications on pole-replacement cost causation and make-ready timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of new rules / applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: These rule amendments apply only to disputes involving pole attachments of a cable television system or a provider of telecommunications service and do not apply to disputes involving pole attachments of a broadband-only Internet service provider, and do not apply to poles owned/controlled by a railroad, the Federal Government, a state (including a political subdivision), or a cooperative association, or where the poles at issue are located in a state (or DC) that has certified it regulates pole attachments pursuant to 47 U.S.C. § 224(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should the Commission reclassify broadband-only Internet service as a telecommunications service, section 224 would apply to broadband-only ISPs. The RBAT and Accelerated Docket reforms are therefore limited to the classes of attachers and poles described above; parties should confirm jurisdictional applicability before seeking RBAT review or Accelerated Docket treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for RBAT review and assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: The RBAT will prioritize the resolution of any pole attachment dispute that a party alleges is impeding or delaying the deployment of broadband facilities (including where the party is also seeking placement of the matter on the Accelerated Docket).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party seeking RBAT review must first notify the Chief of the Enforcement Bureau’s Market Disputes Resolution Division (MDRD) by phone and in writing, then follow directions to submit a streamlined 'Request for RBAT Review and Assessment' form. The RBAT review is available only to attachers and pole owners that are direct parties to the dispute (including their counsel). Notification to MDRD is required prior to filing a formal complaint if the party intends to seek Accelerated Docket inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of Request for RBAT Review and Assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: The form will elicit information relevant to the scope and nature of the dispute and whether the dispute is appropriate for expedited mediation and/or placement on the Accelerated Docket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form will require: identifying information for the parties and services offered; the section(s) of the Act or FCC rule or order alleged to have been violated; a brief description of the dispute (including relation to broadband deployment plans, whether subject to government-funded program deadlines, whether in unserved/underserved area, and harm occurring or likely to occur); the specific relief sought; NDA status; steps taken to resolve the matter; whether parties are amenable to mediation; whether the party intends to seek Accelerated Docket inclusion; and information on suitability for accelerated disposition (e.g., number of poles, number and complexity of claims, likely need for discovery or expert affidavits). The RBAT may request additional information as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: RBAT procedures for assessment and remediation
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a completed request, the RBAT will schedule a meeting with all parties as soon as practicable, may request written responses or documentation, and will provide guidance and advice on effective means of resolving the dispute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The RBAT may recommend an abbreviated mediation process, placement of a complaint (or portion thereof) on the Accelerated Docket, or any other action determined to help parties resolve disputes. The RBAT will distill issues in dispute, identify those most impacting broadband deployment, encourage focus on threshold or urgent issues, and, where appropriate, recommend streamlined proceedings or 'test cases' to narrow disputes. The RBAT has discretion to request relevant information and to shape the process; it will not supplant complaint procedures if mediation fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria guiding RBAT recommendations for Accelerated Docket placement
rubrics_metrics.description: RBAT will determine whether a complaint (or portion thereof) is suitable for accelerated disposition based on a totality of factors, including factors related to whether the dispute 'impedes or delays broadband deployment.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors the RBAT will consider (as reflected in the Request form and discussion) include whether the dispute is connected to active broadband deployment plans or projects, whether the projects are subject to government funding deadlines, whether the dispute arises in unserved or underserved areas, the nature and number of poles at issue, the number and complexity of claims, the likely need for discovery or expert affidavits, and whether the dispute raises relatively straightforward legal/evidentiary issues. Disputes raising straightforward issues are more likely to be placed on the Accelerated Docket; complex disputes may not be suitable for the 60-day Accelerated Docket. The RBAT will apply a 'totality of the criteria' analysis rather than categorical rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shot clocks and timelines (Accelerated Docket and ordinary proceedings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accelerated Docket proceedings are required to be concluded within 60 days. Current rules establish a 180-day deadline for final action on 'pole access complaints' (alleging a complete denial of access) and a 270-day deadline for final action on other pole attachment complaints alleging unjust or unreasonable rates/terms/conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion on the Accelerated Docket shortens pleading deadlines and other procedural rules. A party pursuing RBAT review and Accelerated Docket treatment must make the required notification before filing a formal complaint. Mediation through RBAT does not trigger the 180- or 270-day 'shot clock' deadlines unless a formal complaint is filed; if mediation succeeds no complaint is needed. Parties should choose whether to accept RBAT recommendations and proceed under the schedule established by Commission staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'pole access complaint'
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of the 180-day shot clock, a 'pole access complaint' is a complaint filed by a cable television system or provider of telecommunications service that alleges a complete denial of access to a utility pole, duct, conduit, or right-of-way owned or controlled by a utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition does not encompass complaints alleging that a utility is imposing unreasonable rates, terms, or conditions that amount to a denial of pole access. Parties should frame their pleadings with this distinction in mind when assessing which deadlines apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency requirement — pole inspection and replacement information
rubrics_metrics.description: We require utilities to provide information regarding pole conditions and scheduled replacements to the extent that information is contained in cyclical pole inspection reports that utilities already create and maintain in the ordinary course of their business, or in pole inspection reports created between cyclical reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requirement increases transparency so attachers have information about where poles have been identified for replacement. Commissioner guidance emphasizes this is a 'floor, not a ceiling' — utilities and attachers may share additional information to facilitate deployments. The RBAT and one-touch make-ready rules complement this transparency requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification of 'red tagged' poles and cost causation for replacements
rubrics_metrics.description: We clarify that a 'red tagged' pole is one that the utility has identified as needing replacement for any reason other than the pole’s lack of capacity, and provide additional examples of when a pole replacement is not 'necessitated solely' as a result of a third party’s attachment or modification request (i.e., when a pole already requires replacement at the time the new attacher makes a request).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursuant to section 1.1408(b) and precedent, utilities may not require requesting attachers to pay the entire cost of pole replacements that are not solely caused by the new attacher; utilities may not avoid responsibility for pole replacement costs by postponing replacements until new attachment requests are submitted. Cost-sharing principles apply where modifications benefit multiple parties, and utilities are responsible for replacements undertaken for their own benefit when no other attachers derive a benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on RBAT authority — mediation vs. adjudication
rubrics_metrics.description: The RBAT is designed to assist parties in resolving disputes expeditiously without the need for litigation, but it will not supplant existing complaint procedures; if parties cannot reach resolution, the complaint process (including the Accelerated Docket) remains available to adjudicate disputes in accordance with due process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some commenters suggested RBAT be given authority to resolve disputes without a complaint process; the Commission declined that approach. The RBAT may recommend mediation or Accelerated Docket placement, but any formal adjudication follows existing complaint rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural prerequisites and limitations for seeking Accelerated Docket treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: A complainant that seeks inclusion of a proceeding on the Accelerated Docket must submit a request to the Chief of the Enforcement Bureau’s MDRD, by phone and in writing, prior to filing the complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MDRD Chief will direct the party to the RBAT form. The initial notification constitutes the notification required under section 1.736(b). A prospective complainant may accept RBAT recommendation to proceed on the Accelerated Docket by moving forward with the agreed schedule and process established by Commission staff, with or without the consent of the other party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of dispute focus — active deployment and government deadline sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will focus new procedures on disputes that are interfering with active broadband deployment plans or projects, particularly where projects are subject to government-funded program deadlines or involve unserved or underserved areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This focus aligns the remedy with the goal of timely broadband deployment. Many commenters urged limiting expedited procedures to disputes connected to active deployment. RBAT will therefore prioritize such disputes and weigh program deadlines and harms in its assessment for expedited processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further Notice proposals regarding large orders and make-ready timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The Further Notice seeks comment on whether utilities should have an additional 90 days for make-ready for requests exceeding 3,000 poles or 5 percent of the utility’s poles in a state; whether to add additional make-ready timeline tiers for very large applications; and whether to require that a utility notify an attacher 15 days after receiving a complete application that it cannot conduct the survey within the required 45-day period (making self-help available for the estimate process).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are proposals under the Further Notice; the Commission requests comment on costs and benefits, workforce/contractor constraints, whether attachers face obstacles invoking self-help or one-touch make-ready, and whether utilities should be required to designate an available contractor if they disqualify an attacher-chosen contractor. Information submitted will inform whether revisions to make-ready timelines and self-help rules are necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small-entity/regulatory flexibility considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Further Notice seeks comment on potential reporting, recordkeeping, and compliance obligations on small entities arising from proposals like additional make-ready time for very large requests and other process changes; the Commission requests information on costs and benefits to evaluate impacts on small entities and alternatives under the RFA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission lists RFA-mandated alternatives to consider (differing compliance requirements/timetables, simplification/clarification, performance standards, exemptions) and asks for data (e.g., availability of qualified contractors) to assess economic impacts before adopting rule changes.
